component.notes: Located by glob, never by path depth. The tar layout is not stable across OpenHarmony releases -- setup-ohos-sdk's installer carries per-version strip levels -- so a hardcoded depth breaks on a version bump in a way that looks like a corrupt download.

notes.why_committed: The mirror publishes ohos-sdk-windows_linux-public.tar.gz.sha256 beside the archive, but fetching a checksum from the same server as the artifact verifies transport integrity and nothing else: whoever can change one can change both. This value is committed so every later download is checked against a hash under version control, which is the standard the rest of this repository already holds (see engine/third_party/rusty_v8/*/component-manifest.json and scripts/fetch-v8-archives.sh).
notes.trust_on_first_use: The hash was recorded from the mirror on 2026-08-12 and could not be recomputed independently -- the archive is 3.2 GB and no local copy of it survives the install. So this pin proves the archive has not changed since that date; it does not prove it was correct then. That is the same trust model as any lockfile, and it is stated rather than implied.
notes.why_this_version: 5.1.0.107 (API 18) is the SDK that produced the OpenHarmony artifacts this repository publishes: both librusty_v8-*-linux-ohos.a archives and the staged package manifests record it as build_sdk. Bumping it changes the toolchain identity recorded in every OHOS artifact, so it is a deliberate act, not a convenience.
notes.api_floor_is_separate: This is the SDK used to build, not the API level the package claims to support. The declared floor is MIGO_OHOS_MIN_API (default 20) and is checked against a floor sysroot by scripts/test-ohos-symbol-floor.sh. The two numbers are unrelated on purpose and must not be collapsed.
